- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.1) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 7-day mean.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak.  
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > 0.0) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast.  
- Model tends to lag in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; adjust forecast to align with 3-day moving average of true values.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates mean price when sentiment is weak; apply 1–3% downward correction based on sentiment volatility index (avg abs sentiment > 0.2).  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.4 → +0.1), model misreads momentum; reduce forecast by 1–2% for each reversal cycle.
